To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the factors that influence community members to share their knowledge with others are: 1) perceived reciprocity, 2) trust, 3) knowledge sharing self-efficiency, and 4) perceived relative advantage.

(1) the norm of reciprocity has a positive influence on members' knowledge sharing behavior in PVCs; (2) interpersonal trust and knowledge sharing self-e- ffectiveness have a positive effect on members' knowledge contribution behavior in PVCs, but only the former has a positive effect on knowledge collecting behavior; (3) perceived relative advantage has a positive influence in both knowledge contribution and collecting behaviors; (4) members' knowledge sharing behaviors have a positive influence on their knowledge utilization;

the norm of reciprocity (NORM), interpersonal trust (TRUST), knowledge sharing self-efficiency (KSS-E), perceived relative advantage (PRADV) and knowledge sharing (KS) are the factors that significantly affect knowledge sharing in PVCs; and the KS and collecting behavior are significantly associated with knowledge utilization, while the collecting behaviors are more effective than the contributing behavior in promoting community.
